learn.title: What an angle is
learn.body: An angle is formed by two rays that share an endpoint. The shared endpoint is the vertex and the rays are the sides. We measure an angle in degrees. A full turn around a point is $360^\circ$.

learn.title: Naming an angle
learn.body: We name an angle with three points, and the vertex goes in the middle. $\angle ABC$ has its vertex at $B$. With a protractor, place the centre on the vertex and line one side up with $0^\circ$. Read where the other side crosses the scale.

learn.title: Four kinds of angle
learn.body: An acute angle is between $0^\circ$ and $90^\circ$. A right angle is exactly $90^\circ$. An obtuse angle is between $90^\circ$ and $180^\circ$. A straight angle is exactly $180^\circ$, which looks like a straight line.

learn.title: Angle addition
learn.body: If ray $OB$ lies inside $\angle AOC$, then $\angle AOB+\angle BOC=\angle AOC$.
Before you measure, classify the angle by eye. If it looks acute, your reading must be under $90^\circ$. This catches reading the wrong scale on a protractor.

questions.explanation: Obtuse angles are bigger than $90^\circ$ and smaller than $180^\circ$.

questions.prompt: In $\angle PQR$, which point is the vertex?
questions.explanation: The middle letter of the name is the vertex.

questions.prompt: $\angle AOB=35^\circ$ and $\angle BOC=50^\circ$. Find $\angle AOC$ in degrees.
A full turn around a point is \_\_ degrees.
questions.explanation: A half turn is $180^\circ$ and a quarter turn is $90^\circ$. A full turn is $360^\circ$.

questions.prompt: $\angle AOC=128^\circ$ and $\angle AOB=53^\circ$. Find $\angle BOC$ in degrees.
Match each angle measure to its name.
questions.explanation: Compare each measure with $90^\circ$ and $180^\circ$ to name the angle.
